business.name: Business
business.description: The organisation's capabilities, processes, and operating model — what the business does and why. This domain sets the context that all others serve.

data.name: Data
data.description: The data assets, structures, and governance that support business operations — ensuring data is well-defined, trusted, and available where it is needed.

integration.name: Integration
integration.description: How systems and services connect and communicate — covering APIs, events, messaging, and the rules that govern how information flows between them.

application.name: Application
application.description: The software applications and platforms that deliver business capabilities — what exists, how it is organised, and how it relates to business needs.

solution.name: Solution
solution.description: Joined-up designs that span multiple domains to address a specific business need or initiative — bringing together business, data, integration, and application concerns.

conceptual.name: Conceptual
conceptual.label: What & Why
conceptual.description: Sets the direction — what the architecture needs to achieve and why, independent of any technology choices. In TOGAF terms, conceptual artefacts are Architecture Building Blocks (ABBs).

logical.name: Logical
logical.label: How
logical.description: The rules and principles that guide design decisions, without committing to any specific tool or product. In TOGAF terms, logical artefacts are Architecture Building Blocks (ABBs).

physical.name: Physical
physical.label: Where & With What
physical.description: The concrete standards and technology decisions that govern how the architecture is built and operated. In TOGAF terms, physical artefacts are Solution Building Blocks (SBBs).

catalogue.label: Catalogues
catalogue.description: Structured lists of architecture entities, validated by JSON Schema.

diagram.label: Diagrams
diagram.description: Visual representations of architecture entities and their relationships.

document.label: Documents
document.description: Free-form narrative content authored in Markdown, used for contextual or explanatory artefacts.

matrix.label: Matrices
matrix.description: Grids mapping relationships between entity sets, spanning abstraction layers or domains.

card-based.label: Card Based
card-based.description: Hierarchical nested cards (e.g. Business Capability Model).

process-flow.label: Process Flow
process-flow.description: Sequential chevron flow by level (e.g. Business Process Model).

sequence.label: Sequence
sequence.description: Ordered message / event flow between actors or systems.

timeline.label: Timeline
timeline.description: Roadmap or change over time (e.g. capability evolution plan).

BUS-STR.name: Business Architecture Strategy
BUS-STR.description: A catalogue of strategic goals and direction for the Business domain — the outcomes the organisation is trying to achieve and why.

BUS-CAP.name: Business Capabilities
BUS-CAP.description: A hierarchical catalogue of what the organisation does, structured by capability area and sub-capability.

BUS-BCM.name: Business Capability Model
BUS-BCM.description: A visual map of the organisation's capabilities, arranged as a nested hierarchy.

BUS-PRO.name: Business Processes
BUS-PRO.description: A catalogue of the key processes the organisation runs to deliver business value, structured by type and level.

BUS-BPM.name: Business Process Model
BUS-BPM.description: A sequential chevron flow of the organisation's processes at Level 1 and 2, with per-L1 drill-downs to Level 3.

BUS-CAP-PRO.name: Business Capabilities ↔ Business Processes
BUS-CAP-PRO.description: Maps business capabilities to the processes that realise them at Level 1 and Level 2.

BUS-PRN.name: Business Architecture Principles
BUS-PRN.description: The guiding principles that shape how Business architecture decisions are made.

BUS-STR-PRN.name: Business Architecture Strategy ↔ Principles
BUS-STR-PRN.description: Maps Business Architecture Strategy statements to the Architecture Principles that operationalise them.

BUS-GRD.name: Business Architecture Guardrails
BUS-GRD.description: Rules and minimum standards that must be followed in Business Architecture.

BUS-PRN-GRD.name: Business Architecture Principles ↔ Guardrails
BUS-PRN-GRD.description: Maps Business Architecture Principles to the Guardrails that make them concrete and enforceable.

DAT-STR.name: Data Architecture Strategy
DAT-STR.description: A catalogue of strategic goals and direction for the Data domain.

DAT-DAC.name: Data Domains & Concepts
DAT-DAC.description: The organisation's key data subject areas and the conceptual data entities within each.

DAT-CDM.name: Conceptual Data Model
DAT-CDM.description: A visual map of the organisation's key data concepts and how they relate.

DAT-PRO-DAC.name: Business Processes ↔ Data Domains & Concepts
DAT-PRO-DAC.description: CRUD mapping showing which business processes create, read, update, or delete which conceptual data entities.

DAT-PRN.name: Data Architecture Principles
DAT-PRN.description: The guiding principles that shape how Data architecture decisions are made.

DAT-STR-PRN.name: Data Architecture Strategy ↔ Principles
DAT-STR-PRN.description: Maps Data Architecture Strategy statements to the Architecture Principles that operationalise them.

DAT-GRD.name: Data Architecture Guardrails
DAT-GRD.description: Rules and minimum standards that must be followed in Data Architecture.

DAT-PRN-GRD.name: Data Architecture Principles ↔ Guardrails
DAT-PRN-GRD.description: Maps Data Architecture Principles to the Guardrails that make them concrete and enforceable.

INT-STR.name: Integration Architecture Strategy
INT-STR.description: A catalogue of strategic goals and direction for the Integration domain.

INT-IFC.name: Interface Catalogue
INT-IFC.description: The logical interfaces that connect platforms across the application landscape, and the direction of data flow between them.

INT-WRD.name: Interface Wiring Diagram
INT-WRD.description: Visual map of the integration landscape — platform-to-platform connections with flow counts and per-pair interface drill-down.

INT-DAC-IFC.name: Data Domains & Concepts ↔ Interface Catalogue
INT-DAC-IFC.description: Maps each interface in the Interface Catalogue to the conceptual data entities that flow across it.

INT-PRN.name: Integration Architecture Principles
INT-PRN.description: The guiding principles that shape how Integration architecture decisions are made.

INT-STR-PRN.name: Integration Architecture Strategy ↔ Principles
INT-STR-PRN.description: Maps Integration Architecture Strategy statements to the Architecture Principles that operationalise them.

INT-GRD.name: Integration Architecture Guardrails
INT-GRD.description: Rules and minimum standards that must be followed in Integration Architecture.

INT-PRN-GRD.name: Integration Architecture Principles ↔ Guardrails
INT-PRN-GRD.description: Maps Integration Architecture Principles to the Guardrails that make them concrete and enforceable.

APP-STR.name: Application Architecture Strategy
APP-STR.description: A catalogue of strategic goals and direction for the Application domain.

APP-DAP.name: Application Domains & Platforms
APP-DAP.description: The organisation's application landscape, grouped by business domain and the platforms within each.

APP-DPM.name: Domains & Platforms Model
APP-DPM.description: A visual map of the organisation's application landscape.

APP-CAP-DAP.name: Business Capabilities ↔ Application Domains & Platforms
APP-CAP-DAP.description: Maps each APP-DAP platform to the Level 2 business capabilities it supports.

APP-PRO-DAP.name: Business Processes ↔ Application Domains & Platforms
APP-PRO-DAP.description: Maps which application platforms support which Level 1 business processes.

APP-PRN.name: Application Architecture Principles
APP-PRN.description: The guiding principles that shape how Application architecture decisions are made.

APP-STR-PRN.name: Application Architecture Strategy ↔ Principles
APP-STR-PRN.description: Maps Application Architecture Strategy statements to the Architecture Principles that operationalise them.

APP-GRD.name: Application Architecture Guardrails
APP-GRD.description: Rules and minimum standards that must be followed in Application Architecture.

APP-PRN-GRD.name: Application Architecture Principles ↔ Guardrails
APP-PRN-GRD.description: Maps Application Architecture Principles to the Guardrails that make them concrete and enforceable.

APP-CAT.name: Application Catalogue
APP-CAT.description: The physical applications (vendor products) deployed across the organisation, with their lifecycle status and TIME classification.

APP-DAP-CAT.name: Application Domains & Platforms ↔ Application Catalogue
APP-DAP-CAT.description: Maps each APP-DAP platform to the physical application(s) in APP-CAT that implement it.

SOL-STR.name: Solution Architecture Strategy
SOL-STR.description: A catalogue of strategic goals and direction for the Solution domain.

SOL-PRN.name: Solution Architecture Principles
SOL-PRN.description: The guiding principles that shape how Solution architecture decisions are made.

SOL-STR-PRN.name: Solution Architecture Strategy ↔ Principles
SOL-STR-PRN.description: Maps Solution Architecture Strategy statements to the Architecture Principles that operationalise them.

SOL-GRD.name: Solution Architecture Guardrails
SOL-GRD.description: Rules and minimum standards that must be followed in Solution Architecture.

SOL-PRN-GRD.name: Solution Architecture Principles ↔ Guardrails
SOL-PRN-GRD.description: Maps Solution Architecture Principles to the Guardrails that make them concrete and enforceable.

SOL-AVI.name: Architecture Vision(s)
SOL-AVI.description: TOGAF Phase A: Architecture Vision. One or more architecture vision documents capturing the strategic intent, objectives, drivers, and constraints for a programme or domain — together with the stakeholders involved and the concerns they hold. Multiple instances — one per initiative.

SOL-AIN.name: Architecture Intent(s)
SOL-AIN.description: TOGAF Phase A: Architecture Vision. Structured records of architecture direction before formal ADRs — capturing context, the stakeholders and concerns in play, options considered, and the recommended direction. Multiple instances — one per domain or capability area.

SOL-SVI.name: Solution Intent(s)
SOL-SVI.description: TOGAF Phases B–D: Architecture Definition. The SAFe Solution Intent — the single source of truth for what is being built and why, distinguishing fixed intent (committed requirements and decisions) from variable intent (options still under exploration). High-level solution descriptions per epic or feature — problem statement, solution overview, platforms involved, risks, and assumptions. Multiple instances — one per epic or initiative.

SOL-SDE.name: Solution Design(s)
SOL-SDE.description: TOGAF Phases B–D: Architecture Definition. Detailed logical solution designs per feature — solution components, data flows, UML diagrams (Mermaid/PlantUML), interface requirements, and NFRs. Multiple instances — one per feature or design area.

SOL-ISP.name: Interface Specification(s)
SOL-ISP.description: TOGAF Phases B–D: Architecture Definition (Technology Architecture). Physical-level technical specifications for integration interfaces — protocol, auth, data format, endpoints, data model, error handling, SLA, and test scenarios. Multiple instances — one per interface.
